# 004. Pending-queue default is still 16, the whole default packet pool: d2d95301 changed gen_config.py but the generated files were never regenerated

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | high |
| Category | security |
| Location | [build.rs:16](../build.rs#L16), [gen_config.py:60](../gen_config.py#L60), [Cargo.toml:303](../Cargo.toml#L303), [src/config.rs:90](../src/config.rs#L90), [xarxa-driver/build.rs:9](../xarxa-driver/build.rs#L9), [src/stack.rs:2712](../src/stack.rs#L2712), [src/neighbor.rs:492](../src/neighbor.rs#L492) |
| Features | default |
| Verification | reproduced with a test |

## Summary

Commit d2d95301 set the `pending_queue_count` default to 2 in gen_config.py, because 16 parked packets take the whole default pool of 16 and stall the stack. build.rs, Cargo.toml and src/config.rs were not regenerated, so the effective default is still 16. An on-link attacker can pin every pool buffer with 16 spoofed pings and keep the stack starved by repeating them.

## Details

- gen_config.py:60: `feature("pending_queue_count", default=2, min=1, max=256, pow2=8)`
- build.rs:16 (autogenerated block): `("PENDING_QUEUE_COUNT", 16),`
- Cargo.toml:303: `pending-queue-count-16 = [] # Default`
- src/config.rs:90: `This is a limit with and without \`alloc\`. Default: 16.`
- xarxa-driver/build.rs:9: `("PACKET_BUF_COUNT", 16),`
- `git show d2d95301 --stat`: only gen_config.py changed. Its message: "The previous default (16) matched the default packet buf count (also 16), so if you send 16 packets to an unresolved neighbor would cause a total stack stall."

An ICMP echo request from an unused on-link address gets a reply built in the received buffer. The reply routes on-link, finds no neighbor, and is parked:

src/stack.rs:2712-2714
```rust
NeighborLookup::Pending { next_hop } => {
    debug!("neighbor {} pending, queing packet", next_hop);
    self.pending.push((iface.handle, next_hop), buf, self.now);
}
```

`PendingQueue::push` (src/neighbor.rs:492-503) drops the head only when the `BoundedVec<_, PENDING_QUEUE_COUNT>` is full. Nothing caps parked packets per neighbor. Parked packets stay until resolution fails (3 probes, about 3 s), or until `PENDING_QUEUE_LIFETIME` (5 s, src/neighbor.rs:23) for packets whose neighbor entry was evicted from the 8-entry cache. On real hardware the driver's RX ring also holds pool buffers, so fewer than 16 spoofed packets are enough.

Any local traffic to unresolved neighbors pins buffers the same way, for example a UDP app sending to a dead host.

## Failure scenario

Default build, Ethernet interface 192.168.1.1/24. An attacker on the LAN sends 16 echo requests with spoofed sources 192.168.1.100 to .115, none of which answer ARP. Each reply parks, and together they hold all 16 pool buffers for about 3 s. `PacketBuf::try_new()` fails everywhere: the driver drops RX, TCP and UDP stall, ARP replies and DHCP renewals are not sent. Repeating the burst every few seconds keeps the stack down.

## Reproduction

Test in `mod test` of src/stack.rs, scratch copy of HEAD, with `PendingQueue::packets` made `pub(crate)`. The unit-test pool is 1024 buffers (dev-dependency `packet-buf-count-1024`), so the test counts parked packets rather than showing an empty pool.

```rust
#[test]
fn verify_pending_queue_pins_pool() {
    let (mut stack, rx, _tx) = test_stack(Medium::Ethernet);
    println!("PENDING_QUEUE_COUNT={} PACKET_BUF_COUNT(default driver)=16", crate::config::PENDING_QUEUE_COUNT);
    for i in 0..20u8 {
        let src = Ipv4Addr::new(192, 168, 1, 100 + i);
        let request = icmpv4_echo(Icmpv4Message::EchoRequest, 0x1234, i as u16, b"hello");
        let packet = ipv4_packet(src, OUR_V4, IpProtocol::Icmp, &request);
        inject(&mut stack, &rx, eth_frame_from(OTHER_HW, OUR_HW, EthernetProtocol::Ipv4, &packet));
    }
    let n = stack.inner.pending.packets.len();
    println!("parked={}", n);
    assert!(n < 16, "pending queue holds {} buffers", n);
}
```

`cargo test --lib verify_pending_queue -- --nocapture`:
```
PENDING_QUEUE_COUNT=16 PACKET_BUF_COUNT(default driver)=16
parked=16
panicked at src/stack.rs:6666:9: pending queue holds 16 buffers
```

## Suggested fix

Re-run gen_config.py so build.rs, Cargo.toml and the `Default:` line in src/config.rs say 2. Consider a build-time check that `PENDING_QUEUE_COUNT < PACKET_BUF_COUNT`, and a per-neighbor cap on parked packets.
